en: If [I] go by sea, a corpse soaked in the water;
if [I] go by the mountains, a corpse with grass growing on it:
at the side of the Great Lord, there indeed let [me] die;
rom: Ōkimi no he ni koso shiname
notes: Romanization: modified Hepburn of the words as they are sung, not a letter-by-letter transliteration of the historical kana spelling: かへりみはせじ is sung kaerimi wa seji (へ as e, the particle は as wa). The two-part lines keep the original's space as a plain space.
The subject is not expressed in the Japanese; [I] / [me] are supplied. It may equally be read as 'we'.
line 3: 大君 (Ōkimi), 'the Great Lord', is the sovereign, the emperor; 辺 (he) is 'side, vicinity'. The form shiname (死なめ, after koso) is a resolve or wish: 'let me die', 'I shall die'.
line 4: kaerimi (顧み) is 'looking back'; the line can also be read as 'I will have no regrets' or 'I will not look back to myself'. The sense is disputed only in emphasis.
line 1: mizuku (水漬く) 'soaked in water, sunk in water'; line 2: kusa musu (草生す) 'grass grows (on it)'.
